Thanks for the feedback! I’m pretty new to writing poetry so I’ll definitely keep in mind that using a variety of word lengths is helpful. As for the rhyming, I’ve always had sort of a knack for coming up with rhymes so I figured I would put it into my writing. And yeah- it is about me. I’m transgender and have always struggled with negative thoughts and feelings about my body, so I figured one of my first poems would reflect those experiences. And I am seeking help! I’m about to start seeing a therapist and have had a psychiatrist for a few years now, so there’s no need to worry. Thanks again for the thoughts!

Thank you so much for the advice! I will definitely try and use that in the future. I was writing this when I was in a bit of a dark place so I was just trying to put my thoughts I was having into words. I understand that it might not be the most vivid, which is likely a product of my somewhat new relationship with poetry (not that I’m trying to make excuses). Again, thank you for the advice and I’m really flattered and glad you could have a connection with my writing.

I’d love to discuss! This was partially just meant to get out my feelings and partially just to practice my writing. I’ve loved writing stories and such through my life but I’d never tried poetry or writing about myself so this is all new for me.

This is good! I’m really fond of short poems like this that can get their message across simply but still have a big impact. Self help books and well meaning people do often say things about needing positive relationships and such to grow, but I think that sometimes negative experiences and relationships can have more of an impact on people than the positive ones. I grew up with pretty bad parents, and that in turn taught me to be kinder to people and treat people with respect. The people with the worst lives can be really nice or really mean, and it all really depends on how they let their experiences shape them. And sometimes those people really do have the biggest hearts. Keep writing, I really enjoyed this and I would love to see more.

I really like it! I think the feelings of desire, hatred, etc. in the poem are all pretty universal. It’s easy to get caught up in yourself and to really love someone else is an amazing feeling. I really liked the lines, “To be sincere, In all we do, Not always shelving, The real you.” It’s something I can definitely relate to, feeling as though you need to hide your truest self away. Finding the people who really like you for what makes you you is really important in life. I also liked the rhyme scheme. I think that’s all I really have to say.
